verdict: Leads are growing and cost-per-lead holds; Google tracking needs fixing.
narrative: Over the last 28 days, you received 137 leads at a cost of $16.08 per lead, entirely through Meta — and the trend is moving in the right direction, with leads up 11% week-over-week while cost per lead stayed virtually flat. Google Ads ran $527 in spend over the same window but recorded zero conversions; this is a confirmed tracking failure, not an ad performance issue, and conversion tracking is being repaired so that spend can be properly measured and optimized. Your Google Business Profile also went quiet in the final 7 days of the period, which is being looked into. On the intake side, there is a gap between contacts entering your system and opportunities being created, and that funnel step is being reviewed to make sure no leads are slipping through. Once tracking is restored on Google and the intake gap is closed, you should see a cleaner picture of full-funnel performance and better footing for scaling.

highlights.phrase: leads received this period, all through Meta ads
cost per lead — flat week-over-week, holding efficiently
spent on Google Ads this period with conversions not yet recorded due to a tracking issue

watch_item.issue: Google Ads conversion tracking is not recording leads, meaning $527 in spend this period is unattributed.
watch_item.fix: Tracking is being repaired and offline conversion import is on track to be live by end of September, at which point Google can be properly optimized.
